rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase (AGA)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled (fully covered) units, landlords may raise rent each year by no more than the annual allowable increase (AGA) set by the Rent Board under a Consumer Price Index formula in the Rent Ordinance. The AGA is capped at 5% in any year. Landlords who have banked (unused) AGAs from earlier years are not prevented from implementing a larger increase. The current AGA is 1.6% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027, up from 1.4% the year before. Landlords can petition only for rent increases for completed capital improvements, not planned ones.
rules.key_value: 1.6% allowable annual increase for 3/1/2026–2/28/2027 (1.4% for 3/1/2025–2/28/2026); maximum AGA 5%; dollar increase = base rent x 0.016

coverage.summary: Applies to rent-controlled (fully covered) rental units under the SF Rent Ordinance; partially covered units are treated separately.

rules.effective_date_note: The 1.6% rate applies March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 and is reset each March 1. The passages do not give the date the underlying ordinance first took effect. The sunset_date marks the end of the current rate period only.
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.review_note: The 5% AGA cap comes from a Rent Board summary (p8) of a change to the Rent Ordinance; the passage does not state when that change took effect. Section-level citation is not stated in the passages.
rules.source_notes: Rates are from SF Rent Board pages (p1, p2). The 5% cap is from p8, an official Rent Board summary.
